key_findings: **The Receiver hybrid factory pattern resolves into 6 architectural variants**, not just the single canonical shape BCS-Y-1145 demonstrated. Variants observed: (a) canonical hybrid (8/16 - gated on container+0x50, fast-path direct cache write at +offset, slow-path alloc+ctor with cleanup); (b) inverted hybrid (2/16 - outer param_2!=0 guard added); (c) +0x52-gated variant (2/16 - uses a second flag at +0x52 layered atop +0x50, with queue-aware slow-path allocation); (d) cache-only direct-write (1/16 - no slow-path, no flag check, always fast-path); (e) cache-ensure-then-forward stub (2/16 - ensures cache exists, then forwards to a secondary on the container itself, not cache); (f) complex EventFamily-dispatch wrapper (1/16 - 1694B, wraps a canonical hybrid in RTTI checks + name-buffer marshaling, fans out from EventFamily case 0xCC).

**6 of 16 hybrid factories now resolve to known Receiver classes**: AchievementPoint (BCS-Y-1342 -> BCS-Y-0085), AchievementTitle (BCS-Y-1343 -> BCS-Y-0082), JobChange (BCS-Y-1344 -> BCS-Y-0098), ChangeActorExtraStat (BCS-Y-1346 -> BCS-Y-0118), ChangeActorSubStatModeBorder (BCS-Y-1347 -> BCS-Y-0121), ChangeActorSubStatStatus (BCS-Y-1348 -> BCS-Y-0124). Each Receiver class now has a 2-layer factory surface: (a) heap-factory simple shape if applicable (e.g. BCS-Y-1144 AchievementId), (b) hybrid factory with fast-path optimization via the shared state cache (the 16-entry cluster).

**Cache field layout emerging**: 0xCC=204-byte ReceiverStateCache holds inline state mirrors at observed offsets: +0x44 (AchievementPoint dword), +0x48 (AchievementTitle dword), +0x50 (ChangeActorExtraStat dword), +0xB5 (ChangeActorSubStatModeBorder char), +0xB7 (TBD byte), +0xB8 (VehicleGrade byte per BCS-Y-1145), +0xB9 (TBD byte), +0xBC (TBD dword), +0xC0..0xC9 (10 bytes for ~7-8 different Receivers), +0xC1 (TBD byte), +0xC2..0xC5 (4 bytes TBD), +0xC6 (JobChange byte), +0xC7..0xC8 (TBD 2 bytes), +0xC9 (TBD byte). Closes ~14 of 18 expected cache fields - the remaining 4 are NullActorImpl slot 49 (BCS-Y-1118) which is at a non-cached path + the 2 cache-ensure stubs (which don't write to cache directly) + the complex variant.

**The +0x52 secondary gate flag is a NEW architectural finding**. Two factories (BCS-Y-1348 ChangeActorSubStatStatus + BCS-Y-1349 NamesArray) use container[+0x52] as an outer no-op guard layered atop the +0x50 fast/slow-path gate. Combined with BCS-Y-1346/1347's outer param_2!=0 guard, this reveals the container struct has at least 2 mode-flag bytes (+0x50 immediate-vs-queued, +0x52 enabled-vs-disabled) plus per-receiver-specific input gates. Later work (Z option) could decomp the container ctor to map all the +0x4X..0x5X mode-flag fields.

**The 2 cache-ensure stubs (BCS-Y-1351 + BCS-Y-1352) reveal a different use of the lazy-init helper**. Their bodies discard the cache return value and forward to FUN_007846F0 / FUN_00784760 with the container itself (not cache). The cache-init call is a side-effect to guarantee cache exists when the secondary touches related state. This is a third architectural mode (alongside direct cache write + receiver alloc) where the cache is initialized lazily for other code-paths that depend on its presence.

**The EventFamily case 0xCC factory (BCS-Y-1353) is the only factory with a direct instruction-level caller** (BCS-Y-0588 EventFamilyDispatcher_Case0xCC). The other 15 are reached via function-pointer table dispatch (vftable_A/vftable_B per evidence). BCS-Y-1353 wraps a BCS-Y-1349-shape body in RTTI-gated dispatch context - it's the only factory whose architecture includes an outer-level RTTI verification step. Suggests this is the actor-near-broadcast variant (e.g. 'change-class' or 'change-name' broadcasts to nearby actors), where the dispatcher must verify the target actor type before applying.
